description: A reader's letter in the Star of Mysore describes it as the first agricultural and industrial exhibition held in Mysore, opened to the public on 16 October 1888 in about 70,000 sq ft of sheds, with more than 30,000 exhibits and a hall of items lent by the Maharaja. It later became part of the Dasara festival and recurred annually as the Dasara Exhibition. This is the single entry for a recurring fair, given for its founding year.
notes: One newspaper reader's letter. Some sources give 1880 as the founding year, which the letter disputes. The Wikipedia title was seen in a search result and not opened. No visitor figures found.

name: Central Canada Exhibition
venue: Lansdowne Park (Exhibition Grounds)
description: The Central Canada Exhibition Association was incorporated in March 1888, after local dissatisfaction with the mismanaged Provincial Exhibition, with the backing of Mayor Stewart and Sir John A. Macdonald. The six-day first fair opened at Lansdowne Park on 24 September 1888, with agricultural and industrial exhibits, circus acts and a balloon display. The fair ran annually, except in wartime, until 2010.
notes: Single opened source. Recurring annual fair: founding year only. The source calls Macdonald 'Premier'; he was federal Prime Minister. Livestock and entertainment elements are part of a general agricultural and industrial fair.

name: Exposicion Provincial del Rosario de Santa Fe (Rosario Provincial Exhibition)

description: Organised by the Club Industrial at the urging of Governor José Gálvez, according to a museum publication on the Rosario exhibition of 1888. It included painters, photographers and sculptors, and the publication treats it as a high point of visibility for local artists.
notes: A search summary links it to Paris 1889 selection, which was not confirmed. Venue and dates not found.

name: Western Pennsylvania Exposition (first exposition)

description: The Western Pennsylvania Exposition Society, usually called the Pittsburgh Exposition, proposed the venture in 1885 and held its first exposition in September 1889 on the Allegheny shore, with trade, poultry and automobile shows, orchestras and fashion shows. A web history says it ran annually for two months each autumn until cancelled in 1917. This entry is for the founding year; it recurred.
notes: Thin evidence: one local-history page with no cited source, and search summaries that agree on September 1889 and the 1889 Machinery Hall. A 2012 University of Georgia dissertation on the exposition was seen in search but not opened (core.ac.uk returned 403). Annual run and 1917 end come from the same web page only.

venue: Yamashita Park
description: Organised by the Yokohama city government to mark the city's recovery from the 1923 Great Kanto earthquake, on land made from earthquake rubble at Yamashita Park. The grounds held pavilions of Tokyo, Hokkaido, Taiwan, Korea, Manchuria and Brazil, plus an aquarium, a children's land and army and navy displays. The Yokohama city park history records a reconstruction exposition in the park's boat basin in March 1935, with a whale kept in the water.

The Palestine Symphony Orchestra gave its first concert there, conducted by Arturo Toscanini.

name: Numaish (Hyderabad industrial exhibition)

The Numaish recurred every year, and by the time of the later source it ran for 46 days from New Year at the Nampally exhibition ground.
